summary: Hermann Osthoff (1847–1909) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who founded Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen. He held posts at Leipzig University (around 1875–1877) and Heidelberg University (around 1877–1909).

Hermann Sauppe (1809–1893) worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Zurich (around 1838–1845) and the University of Göttingen (around 1856–1893), and he taught Georg Bühler.

Hermann Wilhelm Ebel (1820–1875) was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (around 1836–1838) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott (around 1838–1840). He later held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (around 1872–1875).

Hermann von Schlagintweit (1826–1882) worked in history and archaeology and other fields. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich around 1845–1849 and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin around 1851–1854.
Hideaki Kimura (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also held a post as a researcher attested in 1995.

Hideaki Nakatani is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, under Yutaka Ochihara, and earned a PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He taught Jonathan A. Silk and was a professor at Kobe Gakuin University in 2003.
Hidehiko Kurita works in religious studies and Japanology. He completed a PhD at Tohoku University and held a post as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University, attested in 2020.
Hideki Kiyoshima (born 1951) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi and held a post as a lecturer at Kindai University, attested in 1989.

Hidenaka Tanaka (1886–1974) worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo around 1906–1909, held a post at Kyoto Women's University around 1952–1961, and taught Yutaka Iwamoto.

Hidenori S. Sakuma studied at the University of Tokyo and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held positions at Shitennoji University (attested 1991–1998), University of Tsukuba (attested 2003–2011), and Taisho University (attested 2008).

Hideo Mineshima (1927–2013) studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at Taisho University around 1948–1953. He was a professor at Waseda University (around 1972–1998, attested 1999) and held posts at Sanko Research Institute (around 1998) and Bunkyo Gakuin University.

Hideo Sakurai (1916–2011) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University around 1940–1943. He held a post as professor emeritus at Komazawa University, attested between 1982 and 1992.

Hideomi Yaita (born 1953) completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University around 1979–1984, working in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a research assistant at Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (around 1986–1995) and lecturer at Taisho University (around 1995–2001).
Hideto Ono (born 1944) studied Buddhist studies and Sinology at Komazawa University around 1963–1972. He held an assistant professor post at Aichi Gakuin University around 1988–1996.
Hidetoshi Yoshizawa specializes in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Taisho University as a researcher, attested between 1998 and 2008, and as a chief research fellow, attested in 2017.

Hideyo Ogawa (born 1954) studied Indology and philosophy at Hiroshima University around 1973–1982. He served at Hiroshima University as an assistant professor (around 1990–1996) and professor (around 1996–2020), and he taught Shinshu Kusumoto.
Hideyuki Matsumori works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a doctoral student at Soka University, attested in 2006, and later served there as an assistant professor, attested in 2015.
Hildegard Diemberger works in Tibetology and religious studies, having studied under Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner. She has taught Michela Clemente, Lobsang Yongdan, and Adrian Zenz.

Himanshu Prabha Ray studied at Panjab University, Cambridge, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, where she later served as associate professor (around 1995–2006). She also held posts at Oxford, the Humboldt Foundation, and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.

Hiram W. Woodward studied at Harvard College (around 1958–1962) and Yale University (around 1967–1975) in history and archaeology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Michigan, University of Vermont, and Walters Art Museum.
